eps.d: 'In the darkness of Nazi occupation the Special Operations Executive fanned the flames of hope and kept alive the flag of freedom. For this alone it deserves remembering.' In 1940, with Adolf Hitler already in command of Europe and planning the invasion of Britain, Winston Churchill appointed a new top-secret organisation to get behind enemy lines, spark revolt and undermine Hitler's Europe from…

Secret Agent gives a fascinating insight into the lives of the agents who risked their lives to fight this secret war. Through the first-hand accounts of these courageous men and women, series reveals the covert world of the SOE: - how the SOE was formed and the operatives were recruited - the daring missions they carried out - the radio and coding systems that kept them in touch with London…

Sabotage meant blowing up trains, bridges and factories whilst subversion meant fostering revolt or guerrilla warfare in all enemy and enemy-occupied countries. By D-Day on 6 June, 1944 SOE had become a feared organisation that could strike the enemy anytime, anywhere. Agent networks now stretched across Occupied Europe, linked to an army of resistance fighters.
